new: The address of the latest published GRS JSON Schema; every Schedule Document holds the same address.
The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of this GRS JSON Schema last changed.
The build time, in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), of the GRS build that wrote this GRS JSON file. This value is only for debugging; to check whether a GRS JSON file is readable, use schemaVersion.
Schedule Data: the MSPDI part, which GRS exports to MSPDI, and the GRS part, which only GRS uses.
Same as MSPDI Project.
Same as MSPDI Calendars.
Same as MSPDI Tasks, except that Task.parentTaskUid and Task.siblingOrder give the WBS tree. GRS makes ID, OutlineLevel, OutlineNumber and Summary from that tree each time GRS writes MSPDI.
Same as MSPDI Resources.
Same as MSPDI Assignments.

The task groups; GRS shows each one as one row in the Task Group Panel and as one Task Group Lane. taskGroupMembers says which tasks each task group holds. On reading an MSPDI file, GRS makes the task groups from the WBS.
Which task group each task belongs to: one entry per task, from taskUid to taskGroupId.
How GRS draws the Task Graphic of each task (shape, colors and outline width): exactly one entry per task.

One record per task that came from an imported MSPDI file: which MSPDI file and which task in that file, so that a later import of the same MSPDI file updates that task instead of adding a copy. A task made in GRS has no record.
The earlier plan: a saved copy of earlier task dates. GRS matches the copy to the current tasks by uid and draws the copy as an outline over the current tasks for comparison.
Comment boxes in the Task Group Lanes. Each comment box points at a task, a highlight box or a free point.
Highlight boxes: rectangles in the Task Group Lanes that mark a range of days over a range of task groups. GRS draws each highlight box with a frame, a fill or both.
How GRS draws the Schedule Document on opening. GRS always writes the keys that always have a value.

Display scale of the drawing in the Schedule Canvas, in percent: at 100 GRS draws every ...Px value as that many CSS pixels, at 50 at half size. This value scales shapes and text together and does not change the App Header, the Command Palette or the browser zoom.

Text size step of the Schedule Canvas: small, medium or large, which are 7.5, 8.75 and 10 CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. The Schedule Document opens at this step; a reader who changes the step edits the Schedule Document.

Width of one calendar day on the Time Axis, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. When GRS fits the Schedule Data to the window, GRS sets this value so that the whole Schedule Data fits the width of the window.
note: fit phrase: "the schedule" became "the Schedule Data" (zoom to fit has no ruled name)

new: Vertical size of the Task Graphics, as a ratio to the default size. 1 is the default size; 2 draws Plan Bars, Actual Bars and Name Labels twice as tall.

How deep task groups with treeState auto open. A top-level task group is depth 1. With value N, task groups down to depth N are open, so GRS shows rows down to depth N + 1; 0 shows only the top-level task groups, closed.
Where the View starts when the Schedule Document opens: notDecided lets GRS choose, placed gives the day at the left edge and the task group at the top edge.
notDecided: no person has chosen a place yet, and GRS chooses one when GRS opens the Schedule Document; placed: the other keys give the place.
The day at the left edge of the View.
Where the left edge falls inside leftEdgeDay, as a part of that day; 0 is the start of the day.
The task group at the top edge of the View. When that task group no longer exists, scrollPosition becomes notDecided.
Where the top edge falls inside that task group, as a part of the step of the task group (the height of the Task Group Lane plus the gap below), not in pixels; 0 is the top of the Task Group Lane.

The span of days, firstDay to lastDay (both included), that fitting the Schedule Data to the window and PNG and SVG export show instead of the whole Schedule Data when isFixed is true. Absent means no fit span.

The last day of the fit span; the fit span includes the column of that day.

Up to four extra clocks. While GRS shows the time of day, GRS shows each extra clock as one more row under the Time Ruler.
The UTC offset of this extra clock.
Whether this clock is the standard-time or the daylight-time zone of the offset of this clock. This value picks the zone name that GRS shows; GRS uses the offset itself all year.
Whether GRS shows the time of day on the Schedule Canvas; the stored date-times keep their time either way. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
Whether GRS shows Plan Bars, apart from isActualVisible. A new Schedule Document starts with true.

Whether GRS draws Dependency Lines. A new Schedule Document starts with true.

Whether GRS draws vertical Date Grid Lines. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
Whether GRS draws the Group Grid Lines between task groups, in the Task Group Lanes and in the Task Group Panel. A new Schedule Document starts with true.

up stacks the tasks of a task group so that the tasks climb to a goal at the upper right; down stacks them so that the tasks descend to a goal at the lower right. A new Schedule Document starts with up.
Whether the theme is monochrome. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
Width of the Task Group Panel, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100.
Whether the number taskGroupPanelWidthPx, instead of a drag of the Panel Divider, sets the width of the Task Group Panel. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
The state of the head of the Task Group Panel (level 0), above all top-level task groups. collapsed draws no task group at all. A new Schedule Document starts with auto.
The Pinned Task Groups: task groups that stay together at the top of the Task Group Lanes, to compare them with task groups far away. Absent means no pinned task group.
How GRS shows the three tables: the Search Window, the Delay Diagnostics Report Window and the Resource List Window.

Whether the Schedule Filter of this table is on; while the Schedule Filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Lanes only what the checked rows of this table select. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
The tasks whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.
The column filters of the Search Window tables (the task table and the comment box table), one per filtered column, by the column names of those tables. Absent means no column has a filter.
How GRS sorts this table. Absent means the default order.

Whether the Schedule Filter of this table is on; while the Schedule Filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Lanes only what the checked rows of this table select. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
The tasks whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.
The column filters of the table of the Delay Diagnostics Report Window, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column has a filter.
How GRS sorts this table. Absent means the default order.
How GRS shows the table of the Resource List Window: Schedule Filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.

Whether the Schedule Filter of this table is on; while the Schedule Filter is on, GRS draws in the Task Group Lanes only what the checked rows of this table select. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
The resources whose row has a check in the show column of this table. Absent means no row has a check.

The column filters of the table of the Resource List Window, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column has a filter.

The Document Stamp: the time of the last change and of the last save, and who wrote the Schedule Document last.
The Change Log: notes that people or an AI write about changes to the Schedule Document, oldest first. A new entry goes at the end.

Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerDay: the length of one working day (1d) in minutes, {{S-128}} when absent. GRS warns on opening the Schedule Document if the working times of any working day add up to a total other than this value.
Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerWeek.
Same as MSPDI Project/DaysPerMonth.
Same as MSPDI Project/WeekStartDay, where 0 is Sunday. Absent means Monday (1).

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultStartTime: the time of day GRS gives a start that has a date and no time (the start of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualStart, resume, project.startDate); {{S-482}} when absent. A milestone's start gets defaultFinishTime instead.

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultFinishTime: the time of day GRS gives a finish that has a date and no time (the finish of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualFinish, stop, deadline, project.statusDate); {{S-483}} when absent. A milestone's start gets this time as well.
The hue of the theme, in degrees. Every color written as {"kind":"theme"} uses this hue. A new Schedule Document starts with 214.

How many working days the progress point of a parent task may lie outside the progress points of the work below the parent task, before Delay Diagnostics asks whether an update is missing. A new Schedule Document starts with 1.
One counter for the uids of tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. GRS never reuses a uid, so a new uid is always above this value.
How many times GRS has imported an MSPDI file into this Schedule Document; 0 means never. GRS compares TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportNumber with this number.
The OutlineLevel at which the tasks of an imported MSPDI file start (not counting the project summary task); export writes from this number. A new Schedule Document starts with 1.

The format the Schedule Document came from: grs for a Schedule Document made in GRS, pj12 or pj15 for an MSPDI file (pj15 when the file has any element that only pj15 has). GRS does not write this value to MSPDI.
Carried MSPDI values of this element, under their MSPDI names.
Carried MSPDI elements under this one; GRS writes each element back in the same place.
Same as MSPDI Calendar.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/UID.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/BaseCalendarUID: the calendar this one inherits from. GRS keeps the value but does not inherit: GRS counts only the days this calendar itself lists.
The order of the calendar as in the MSPDI file; GRS writes the calendars back in that order.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/Name.
Same as MSPDI Calendar/IsBaseCalendar. Absent reads as false.

Carried MSPDI elements under this one; GRS writes each element back in the same place.

The order of this weekday within the calendar, as in the MSPDI file.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/DayType, where 1 is Sunday, except that the value is never 0: Exception holds the exception days.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/DayWorking. Absent reads as not working.
Same as MSPDI WeekDay/WorkingTimes. Absent on a working day means the default spans {{S-580}}.
Carried MSPDI values of this element, under their MSPDI names.
Carried MSPDI elements under this one; GRS writes each element back in the same place.

The order of this exception within the calendar, as in the MSPDI file.
Same as MSPDI Exception/Name.

Same as MSPDI Exception/TimePeriod/ToDate: the last day of the exception, included. GRS reads only the date and writes T23:59:00.
Same as MSPDI Exception/DayWorking. Absent reads as not working.

Same as MSPDI Exception/Type. GRS counts only a one-off exception: recurrenceKind is 9 or absent, or is 1 and recurrencePeriod is absent or 1; GRS keeps the others unchanged without counting them. Write 1 for an exception you add.
Same as MSPDI Exception/Period.
Same as MSPDI Exception/WorkingTimes. Absent on a working day means the default spans {{S-580}}.
Carried MSPDI values of this element, under their MSPDI names.
Carried MSPDI elements under this one; GRS writes each element back in the same place.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime. GRS refuses spans of one day that overlap or do not start before they end; spans that only touch, such as one ending at 12:00 and one starting at 12:00, are fine.
The order of this span within the day; GRS writes the spans in the order of their start.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime/FromTime.
Same as MSPDI WorkingTime/ToTime. 00:00:00 means 24:00, the end of the day.

Same as MSPDI Task. GRS reads the progress state with these checks, first match wins: no actualStart, not started; actualFinish set, finished; resumeValid false, suspended with no resume date; resume set, suspended with a resume date; otherwise in progress.
Same as MSPDI Task/UID.
The parent task in the WBS. Absent means a top-level task.
Same as MSPDI Task/CalendarUID, the calendar of this task alone. GRS keeps the value and writes the value back, but counts working days with project.calendarUid only.
The order of this task among the tasks under the same parent task.
Same as MSPDI Task/Name.
Same as MSPDI Task/Notes.
Same as MSPDI Task/Start. GRS does not open a GRS JSON or MSPDI file in which a task has no start.
Same as MSPDI Task/Finish. GRS does not open a GRS JSON or MSPDI file in which a task has no finish.
Same as MSPDI Task/Milestone. Absent reads as false. When true, TaskVisual holds milestoneShape; otherwise TaskVisual holds taskShape.
Same as MSPDI Task/Deadline.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualStart. Absent means the task is not started.
Same as MSPDI Task/Stop: the end of the actual work so far on a task that is in progress or suspended. On a finished task actualFinish holds that end; GRS empties stop when GRS finishes a task.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualFinish. Present only on a finished task; a percentComplete of 100 does not mean finished.
Same as MSPDI Task/Resume: on a suspended task, the planned restart of the remaining work.
Same as MSPDI Task/ResumeValid. On a task with actualStart and no actualFinish, false means suspended with no resume date, and GRS does not use a date in resume.

Same as MSPDI Task/PercentComplete, except that GRS recalculates the value as actual working time (actualStart to actualFinish, or to stop) over planned working time (start to finish), times 100, rounded, with no cap at 100. With no planned working time, as on a milestone, the value is 100 once actualFinish is present, else 0.

Calendar days over which GRS fades the start of the Plan Bar, to show that the start is not firm. Rectangle: the start edge slants. Chevron: sets the start notch depth. GRS ignores the value on other shapes. Absent: no fade (a chevron keeps the default depth). 0: a flat start. GRS writes the value to MSPDI as a Task/ExtendedAttribute.
As fadeInCalendarDays, for the finish (on a chevron, the tip depth). GRS writes the value to MSPDI as a Task/ExtendedAttribute.

The id of the task group.
The parent task group. Absent means a top-level task group (depth 1).
The task that this task group represents in the WBS. Absent means the task group represents no task. This property does not decide the name of the task group.
The order of this task group among the task groups under the same parent.
The task group name. Absent means an unnamed task group; GRS shows an empty title. GRS never copies a task name into this property after the task group exists.

Whether the task group is open, closed or hidden in the Task Group Panel. auto follows documentSettings.taskGroupAutoExpandDepth; temporarilyExpanded stays open until the next Zoom to Fit or vertical zoom out, and then becomes auto.
The name of the group that may edit this task group. When present, GRS refuses edits to the tasks in this task group. Absent means anyone may edit.
The color of the Task Group Lane of the task group. Absent means GRS draws no color; {"kind":"theme"} draws the theme color.
Lowest height of the Task Group Lane of the task group, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100; absent means no lowest height. verticalZoomRatio does not change this height.
The URL the task group links to. Absent means no link.
The title of the task group link. Absent means no title.

The task; each task is in exactly one entry.
The task group that GRS draws the task in.

The task that GRS draws with this TaskVisual; each task has exactly one TaskVisual.
Shape of the Task Graphic of a task that is not a milestone. Present exactly when Task.milestone is not true; a milestone holds milestoneShape instead.
Shape of the Milestone Mark. Present exactly when Task.milestone is true.

The fill color of the Plan Bar. Absent means GRS draws no fill; fill and stroke may not both be absent. A custom color may give only one of light and dark: GRS works out the other when GRS opens the Schedule Document.
Outline color of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar. Absent means GRS draws no outline.
Outline width of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar of the task, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS writes 1 for a new task.
Where an imported task came from, so that importing the same MSPDI file again updates the task instead of adding a copy.
The imported task in this Schedule Document.
Project/UID of the MSPDI file that GRS imported this task from. Absent when that MSPDI file had none.
The UID of the task in the MSPDI file that GRS imported the task from.
The id of the import that brought the task in; every import makes a new one. This id stands in for sourceProjectId when the MSPDI file had no Project/UID.
The project.lastImportNumber of the last import that found this task in the imported MSPDI file.
One task of an earlier plan, which GRS matches to the current task by uid and draws only as an outline over the current task.

The task name in the earlier plan.

One comment box. The Leader Anchor of the comment box stands at a free point (an instant, a task group and a height within the Task Group Lane of that task group) or at one of eight points of the task or highlight box that the comment box snapped to.
The id of the comment box.

Where the Leader Line of the comment box points: a free point in the Task Group Lanes, or a point of a task or highlight box that the Leader Line snaps to. A snapped Leader Anchor also keeps a fallback place, which GRS uses when the target of the Leader Anchor no longer exists.
Offset from the Leader Anchor to the lower-left corner of the comment box body, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS scales the offset with displayScalePercent but not with zoom.
The horizontal part of bodyOffsetPx. A positive value moves the box to the right.
The vertical part of bodyOffsetPx. A positive value moves the box down, as in GRS.
The text of the comment box. Absent means an empty body.
Fill color of the comment box body; fillTransparencyPercent 100 draws no fill.
Transparency of the comment box fill in percent: 0 is opaque, 100 draws no fill.
Color of the comment box border and Leader Line.
Width of the comment box border and Leader Line, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS scales the width by displayScalePercent, not by zoom. GRS writes 1 when placing a box.
Color of the comment box text.
Size of the comment box text, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS scales the size by displayScalePercent, not by zoom. GRS writes 10 when placing a box.
The URL that the comment box links to. Absent means no link.
The title of the comment box link. Absent means no title.
Where the Leader Line of a comment box points; kind selects a free point, a task or a highlight box.
freePoint: a place in the Task Group Lanes tied to nothing; task: one of eight points of a Task Graphic; highlightBox: one of eight points of a highlight box.
The point in time where the Leader Anchor stands on the Time Axis.
The task group whose Task Group Lane holds the Leader Anchor; in a fallback, the task group where the Leader Anchor goes when the target of the Leader Anchor no longer exists.
The height of the Leader Anchor within the Task Group Lane of that task group: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom edge.
The uid of the task that the Leader Anchor snaps to.
Which part of the Task Graphic the Leader Anchor snaps to: the Plan Bar, the Actual Bar or the Milestone Mark.
Which of the eight points of the target the Leader Anchor snaps to: the four corners and the middles of the four sides.
Where the Leader Anchor goes when the task no longer exists.
The id of the highlight box that the Leader Anchor snaps to.
Where the Leader Anchor goes when the highlight box no longer exists.
Where the Leader Anchor goes when the target of the Leader Anchor no longer exists: the task group, and the height in the Task Group Lane of that task group.
One highlight box. Encloses a range of dates and task groups.
The id of the highlight box.
The task group at the top edge of the box.
The task group at the bottom edge of the box.
The first day that the box covers (included), as a day in the Schedule Data time zone (project.scheduleDataTimeZone).
The last day that the box covers (included).
Corner radius of the highlight box, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100; 0 gives square corners. GRS scales the radius by displayScalePercent, not by zoom. GRS writes 4 when placing a box.

Border width of the highlight box, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. GRS scales the width by displayScalePercent, not by zoom. GRS writes 1 when placing a box.
When the Schedule Document last changed, when GRS last saved the Schedule Document, and who last wrote the Schedule Document.

When the Schedule Document last changed, in the Schedule Data or in documentSettings.

Terms:
GRS is GoodRelax Scheduler, which opens and edits a Schedule Document and reads and writes GRS JSON files, the format that this GRS JSON Schema defines.
MSPDI (Microsoft Project XML Data Interchange) is the XML file format that Microsoft Project uses. GRS can also read and write MSPDI (.xml) files.
"Same as MSPDI X" indicates that the property has the same meaning and values as MSPDI element X. The description of that property notes any GRS-specific difference.
Concepts:
WBS is the tree of parent and child tasks, as in MSPDI.
Task groups are GRS's own objects that let GRS draw several tasks in one Task Group Lane. Each task belongs to exactly one task group.
GRS counts working days using a single calendar: the calendar that project.calendarUid names.
"Carried" means GRS does not use the value, but preserves the value and writes the value back to MSPDI unchanged.
Actual dates are the authoritative source of task progress. GRS decides from the actual dates of a task whether the task is not started, in progress, suspended, or finished. GRS recalculates percentComplete from those dates when GRS opens a GRS JSON file.
The shape of GRS JSON:
$schema           Address of this GRS JSON Schema
schemaVersion     Version of the shape
buildVersion      GRS build that wrote the GRS JSON file
schedule          Schedule Data
  +- MSPDI part: project, calendars, tasks, resources, assignments (same as MSPDI)
  +- GRS part: taskGroups, taskGroupMembers, taskVisuals, taskOrigins,
     baselineTasks, commentBoxes, highlightBoxes
documentSettings  Document Settings: how GRS draws the Schedule Document on opening
documentStamp     Document Stamp: last change, last save and last writer
changeLogEntries  Change Log: notes on changes
A property with no value is absent: never write null or [].
